speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I can see you have a rash and some flu-like symptoms. To help me narrow this down, have you noticed any specific pattern to the rash, such as spots between your fingers or on your palms? Also, have you had any eye redness or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: That facial rash sparing the mouth area is a very specific clue. Given her age and the progression from a cold-like illness to a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, are your joints or lymph nodes swollen or painful? Also, has anyone around her been diagnosed with the same illness recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming those details. To further assess the extent of the infection and rule out other viral exanthems, could you tell me if you have noticed any joint swelling or stiffness? Additionally, please REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count and REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Rash_Photos.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of a cold-like prodrome, a facial rash sparing the nose, and a subsequent pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities is highly suggestive of Roseola Infantum (exanthem subitum), caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 or 7. Given the age and specific progression, what is the highest fever you reached before the rash appeared, and is the rash currently fading?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum)
